commits.message:
refactor(node-seam): lift Console saveText/saveHtml + prompt readline out of main barrel (rich-demo-site-pek.3.4) (#50)

* refactor(node-seam): lift Console saveText/saveHtml + prompt readline out of main barrel (rich-demo-site-pek.3.4)

The Console.file: type widened from NodeJS.WritableStream to a structural
ConsoleSink ({ write(chunk): unknown }) — exactly the surface Console + Live
actually exercise. That single narrowing collapses six demo-site casts, the
defineProperty(consoleOut, "width") hacks at three sites (folded into a new
getSize option on Console), and the vite resolve.alias stubs for fs and
node:readline that previously papered over the boundary.

saveText/saveHtml moved to src/node/save.ts (consume Console.exportText /
exportHtml). The prompt renderable drops node:readline in favor of an `ask`
PromptInput capability passed via options; the readline binding lives in
src/node/prompt.ts as `nodeAsk`. examples/_browser-shell/node-stub.js is
gone and vite.config.demos.ts no longer aliases node modules — any future
top-level fs/readline regression now fails loud at bundle time, which is
the point.

Verification:
- lint: clean
- vitest: 1748 passed
- demos:build: 10 demos bundled cleanly
- e2e (playwright): 10/10 demos boot with no console.error
- saveHtml end-to-end via EXPORT_HTML=... npm run themes-and-color-studio

* refactor(node-seam): address review — single-enforcer browser-sink check, doc fixes, dead-field removal

- Console: add `defaultSink(useStderr)` trust-boundary helper. The `file`
  getter and `_write` fallback both route through it, throwing a clear
  actionable error when `process` is undefined instead of the opaque
  `ReferenceError: process is not defined` deep inside `_write`.
  [LAW:single-enforcer] keeps the two consumers identical; no second copy
  of the check to drift.
- Prompt: drop dead `console?: Console` field from `PromptOptions` — the
  original `ask()` accepted it as `_options?.console` but never read it.
  Public surface now matches actual behavior, and the type-only `Console`
  import goes with it.
- Prompt: doc now says input is required per call and cites
  [LAW:no-shared-mutable-globals] as the reason there is no
  module-level default. Error message references the correct package
  name `@promptctl/rich-js/node/prompt`.
- node/prompt: module doc shows the correct call signature —
  `Prompt.ask(promptText, { ask: nodeAsk })`.
- host-stream: docstring no longer promises a boolean return — narrowed
  prose to match `ConsoleSink.write(chunk): unknown`, with a note that
  this implementation returns `true` for Node-stream parity but callers
  may not rely on it.
- coverage allowlist: re-sort new entries within their blocks per ASCII
  order (PromptInput/PromptOptions between PrettyOptions and RowLevel;
  lowercase nodeAsk at the end of the renderables-gallery block).

Lint, full vitest, demos:build, and the playwright headless gate all
remain green.

* docs(prompt): finish the package-name + PromptInput contract pass

Two follow-ups from the second review pass:

- Module doc in src/renderables/prompt.ts now uses the full
  `@promptctl/rich-js/node/prompt` specifier. The runtime error and
  node helper doc got this in pass 1; the module-level doc was missed.
- `PromptInput` doc now matches the renderable's actual behavior — the
  trailing space is always appended by `ask()` (single enforcer), so
  implementations should not add their own. Keeps the four prompt
  classes consistent without each having to re-implement the convention.

* chore(coverage): keep allowlist live-progress-console block alphabetical

ConsoleOptions sorts before ConsoleSink (ASCII: 'O' < 'S'). Suppressed
Copilot finding from review pass 3 — no thread to resolve, the commit
is the record.

* refactor: tighten PromptInput contract + skip dead getTerminalSize call

Both findings from review pass 4 — constraint-design wins, not patches:

- Prompt API: `ask` is now a required positional parameter, not an
  optional in `PromptOptions`. The old shape allowed `Prompt.ask("name?")`
  at the type level and always threw at runtime — the type was lying.
  The new shape `Prompt.ask(promptText, input, options?)` makes the
  missing-capability state unrepresentable, and the runtime
  `missingInput()` helper collapses out because the type system now
  enforces what the body was checking. [LAW:types-are-the-program] —
  the implementation is residue once the constraint is right.
  No real callers were affected — only the rich-explore coverage
  renderer references the Prompt classes (typeof check, never invoked).

- Console.resolveGetSize: return a *different* closure for the all-static
  case. When both `width` and `height` are provided at construction, the
  returned function is a constant `() => fixed` — no `getTerminalSize()`
  call (and no `process.env`/`process.stdout` read) on every size read.
  Mixed cases keep the existing dynamic closure. [LAW:dataflow-not-
  control-flow] — the variability lives in which closure was captured at
  construction time, not in branches per call.

Lint, full vitest, demos:build, and the playwright headless gate all
remain green.

* fix: freeze constant size object + sync nodeAsk doc example

Both findings from review pass 5:

- src/core/console.ts: Object.freeze the captured fixed-size object in
  resolveGetSize's all-static path. Without this, a caller could mutate
  console.size and silently change every subsequent read — a divergence
  from the dynamic-closure path (which allocates a fresh object per call
  and is therefore implicitly safe to expose). [LAW:one-source-of-truth]
  — both paths now share the same immutability guarantee.

- src/node/prompt.ts: doc example uses the new positional signature
  `Prompt.ask("What's your name?", nodeAsk)` and shows a second form
  with options. (Missed this in pass 4 when the signature changed.)

* fix(prompt): restore trust-boundary guard + rename save out

Two findings from review pass 6:

- src/renderables/prompt.ts: re-add the `typeof input !== "function"`
  trust-boundary check that I overcorrected away in pass 4. The type
  forbids the bad state for TS callers, but the public API is reachable
  from JS and from `any`-laundered TS — per CLAUDE.md's no-defensive-
  null-guards LAW, system boundaries warrant validation. The throw
  points at the node helper so JS consumers get the same diagnostic
  experience TS consumers don't need. The message uses TypeError
  rather than Error to align with the value-type-mismatch shape, and
  is strictly more correct than the old `!input` truthy check (also
  catches non-function objects, not just nullish values).

- src/node/save.ts: rename the parameter from `console` to `out` in
  saveText and saveHtml. Drops the shadowing of the global console
  object and reads naturally with the demo's `saveHtml(demo.out, ...)`
  and the test's `saveText(c, ...)` call sites.

* chore(coverage): keep allowlist live-progress-console block alphabetical (saveText)

Pushed saveText to the end of the live-progress-console block per
ASCII ordering (lowercase 's' > uppercase letters), matching the
pattern in other blocks. Suppressed Copilot finding from review
pass 7 — no thread to resolve.

* docs: update console/prompt docs for the node-seam API change

Three findings from review pass 8 — all stale-doc consequences of the
public API changes:

- docs/console.md: Exporting section now uses
  `saveText`/`saveHtml` from `@promptctl/rich-js/node/save`. Removed
  `exportSvg`/`saveSvg` lines — neither exists in src/, the doc was
  already lying about them.
- README.md: same update for the recording snippet, with a one-line
  callout explaining why `saveText`/`saveHtml` live on a subpath
  (browser-safety of the main barrel).
- docs/prompt.md: rewritten so every example passes `nodeAsk` as the
  second positional argument matching the new `Prompt.ask(text, input,
  options?)` signature. Added an "Input capability" section explaining
  the design, and a "Custom input sources" section showing the test
  fake pattern. The old "Customization" section that talked about
  overriding nonexistent `process()`/`render()` methods was replaced —
  pre-existing inaccuracy easier to fix during the rewrite than to
  leave standing.

Capture API bug (raised in pass 7 again as suppressed finding 1) tracked
separately in lit `rich-demo-site-pek.6` — pre-existing dead code with
no callers and a design question (redirect vs tee) that doesn't belong
in this PR.

* docs(prompt): align module doc with actual `input` parameter name

Module-level comment said the required positional parameter was named
`ask`, but the public API uses `input: PromptInput`. Doc now matches.

* docs: fix clear-knob direction + add missing imports to prompt snippet

- docs/console.md: the buffer-clear knob description was backwards.
  `exportText`/`exportHtml` default `clear: true` (and `saveText`/
  `saveHtml` forward the option), so the actionable knob is
  `{ clear: false }` to preserve the buffer for a second export
  (e.g. saving both .txt and .html from one recorded run). Doc now
  reflects that.
- docs/prompt.md: "Custom input sources" snippet now imports
  `Prompt` and `Confirm` alongside the `PromptInput` type, so the
  block is genuinely self-contained and copy-pasteable.

* docs(prompt): make Basic string prompt snippet self-contained

Snippet referenced `console.print(...)` without instantiating a Console.
Now imports Console + Prompt + nodeAsk, constructs an `out` Console,
and uses `out.print(...)`. Each example block stands alone — matching
the convention adopted in "Custom input sources".

* docs(README): use the scoped package name in all import specifiers

The README had 13 `from "rich-js"` imports and an `npm install rich-js`
command — but package.json declares the published name as
`@promptctl/rich-js`. Both forms would fail when a user copy-pasted them,
making the README a worse onboarding artifact the larger it got. Now
every import statement and the install command use the scoped name.

Title and prose references to "rich-js" (the project display name) are
left alone — those aren't package-specifier copy/paste hazards.

fix(coverage): label every allowlist entry by its actual export kind

Copilot review on PR #35 flagged that the reason string for KeyEvent
called it a "type" when src/widgets/types.ts declares it as a class.
A reader debugging a coverage failure consumes that reason string
verbatim — a wrong label is misleading guidance, not just imprecision.

The same pattern was repeated across many entries (I had labeled most
interfaces as "type" and several classes as "type"). Rather than
fix only the entry Copilot named, a derivation pass over src/ rewrote
every reason string from the actual export declaration:

  - class      → "<scope>: <Name> class"
  - interface  → "<scope>: <Name> interface"
  - type       → "<scope>: <Name> type alias"
  - const      → "<scope>: <Name> constant"
  - function   → "<scope>: <Name> function"
  - enum       → "<scope>: <Name> enum"

83 lines of labels updated. Existing parenthetical context (e.g.
"used transitively via Pretty") is preserved.

[LAW:one-source-of-truth] The src/ declaration is the canonical
description of an export's kind. A reason string that disagrees with
it is a divergent copy — fix the divergence by deriving from the
source, not by patching the copy point-by-point.

Verification: npm run lint clean; coverage verifier still green
(4/4).

chore(demos): retire flagship-per-domain spec and typing

Removes the artifacts that encoded the over-fit "exactly five flagships
with strict source-module ownership" model the previous demo-tune-up
design produced. The lit epic (rich-demos-l2x) has already been
rewritten back to the user's original ask (dedupe / expand / consolidate
/ reorganize / tweak — fewer + more interesting demos, with existing
working demos preserved until something better replaces them).

# Changes

- **Deleted `spec/demos.md`** — the 392-line spec that defined five
  flagships with rigid source-module ownership and mandated deleting the
  interactive TUIs (rich-explore, claude-sessions) to satisfy the count.
  Retired in favor of judgment-driven concrete improvements.

- **`test/coverage/coverage-allowlist.ts`** — dropped the `Flagship`
  string-literal union, the `burndown(flagship)` helper, and the
  discriminated-union `AllowlistEntry` (`{ kind: "burndown" }`
  vs `{ kind: "permanent" }`). Collapsed to one flat shape:
  `AllowlistEntry { reason: string }`. Per-flagship comment headers
  replaced with factual "-- from src/X --" sectioning. [LAW:absorbed-variance]
  — the discriminated union only had one realized case (burndown);
  collapse to one shape.

- **`test/coverage/coverage.test.ts`** — softened the file header
  comment (no longer claims to be "the keystone" of an epic; explicitly
  notes the verifier is a *floor*, not a quality measure). Updated the
  error messages and the redundant-entry detail to match the new
  AllowlistEntry shape.

- **`examples/themes-and-color-studio/index.ts`** — header comment no
  longer calls the demo "the flagship"; describes what it actually is
  (a printed-tour reference kept for the color subsystem, not a template
  for future demos). One-liner inside main() and one in-line infra
  comment updated to match.

# Verification

- npm run lint: clean
- npx vitest run: 8838 passed | 7 skipped (328 files)
- npm run themes-and-color-studio: runs to completion

# What is NOT changed

No demos under `examples/` are deleted. All existing demos
(`rich-explore`, `claude-sessions`, `rich-themes`, `rich-themes-transposed`,
`rich-theme-designer`, `rich-colors`, `rich-config`, `dropdown-demo`,
`rich-dash`, `rich-markup-plugins`, `rich-strip`, `rich-template-bindings`,
`themes-and-color-studio`, `shared`) remain on disk; their npm scripts
remain wired. Per parent epic non-goal: working demos are not deleted
before something concrete has replaced them and been judged a
replacement.
